title: Very near to you (Tanya, title page)
hook: the Tanya's subtitle is "the word is very nigh unto thee" (Deuteronomy 30:14)
tomorrow: why can't a sad wrestler win? the Tanya has an answer.

segments.voice: Yesterday, the beinoni: the in-between one who feels the pull and never acts on it. Feelings aren't deeds. Before that, Miriam by the river, Bityah at the basket, four children at one table, a margin left open, and later voices pulling up chairs.

Somewhere in a phone there is usually a someday list: the call to make when there's time, the habit for after exams, the thing to learn once life calms down. Someday keeps everything at arm's length. So, yesterday's question: how far away is the good you're reaching for, really? The Tanya answers before its first chapter, on the title page, with a verse.
screen: `THE SOMEDAY LIST.` → `HOW FAR AWAY, REALLY?` → `THE ANSWER ON THE TITLE PAGE.`

segments.voice: The verse is from Moses' last speeches in Deuteronomy: "But the word is very nigh unto thee, in thy mouth, and in thy heart, that thou mayest do it." Just before it, the Torah says the commandment isn't up in heaven, and it isn't across the sea. The Tanya's title page says the whole book is built on that verse, to explain how it is very near, by a long way and by a short way. That's the thing to tell a friend tonight: a book of Hasidic teaching opens by promising that the good is close, and then spends its pages showing how. Look at the three places the verse names. In your mouth: what you say. In your heart: what you feel. That thou mayest do it: what your hands do. Yesterday's beinoni lives right here. The heart may pull the wrong way, yet the mouth and the hands are near enough to choose. And look back at two weeks of lessons: Miriam's hope, Bityah's open arms, an answer sized for one child. None of it needed a mountain. It was a sentence, a feeling, a step.
screen: `NOT IN HEAVEN, NOT ACROSS THE SEA.` · `THE TITLE PAGE'S PROMISE.` · `MOUTH, HEART, HANDS.` · `A SENTENCE, A FEELING, A STEP.` · then, large: `VERY NEAR TO YOU.`

segments.voice: Name one good thing you've been keeping on the someday list: a call, an apology, a habit, a page of study. Find its nearest piece, a sentence you could say or one small thing your hands could do. Decide exactly when, and see yourself doing it.
screen: `ONE THING ON THE SOMEDAY LIST.` · `ITS NEAREST PIECE.` · `DECIDE WHEN.`

segments.voice: Very near to you: the verse on the Tanya's title page. The good is in your mouth, in your heart, and within reach of your hands.
Your line: very near to you. In your mouth, in your heart, in your hands. Two weeks, done.
